chapters.title: The Boy at the Door — Limits and Conditions
chapters.source_excerpt: (27) His eyes overflowed with tears, and so he broke off his speech, took leave of the people, rose, and set out on his journey. The people wept at the warmth and the eloquence of his sermon, and they wished to rise with him; but their reply, in order to preserve courtesy, was to celebrate with him in all this. They did not know what they had agreed to do, so they went off to their houses. He was followed by a youth…

chapters.title: The World, the Hereafter, and the Speech of Parables
chapters.source_excerpt: (94) The boy said: This world, in which this great creation was set, has many people — both the first and the last — who differ concerning it. Some have entrusted themselves to the world and sought it, and saw no merit except in multiplying it. Others reproach it and practice asceticism within it, neither dispensing with it entirely, even though all that is forbidden is much, while only a little of it is forbidden…

chapters.title: Three Layers of Knowledge
chapters.source_excerpt: (154) The boy said: "Are not this world and the Hereafter a pair, and the soul and the body a pair, and the knowledge of the apparent and of the subtle a pair, and so on — many pairs, all of them?" (155) The scholar said: "I accept. But are they pairs of a single kind?" (156) The boy said: "The pairs indicate the religion of Allah." (157) The scholar said: "I accept. chapters.title: Homecoming, the Father, and the Debate with Abu Malik
